study_identification_part.si_4_title: Structural variability of the cerebral cortex in schizophrenia and its association with clinical symptoms

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: This study used data from seven sites: AMC (Asan Medical Center), JNUH (Jeonbuk National University Hospital), COBRE, NMorphCH, MCIC, fBIRN, and UCLA (CNP). AMC and JNUH are Korean hospital datasets. NMorphCH and fBIRN are multi-site consortium datasets without unique names in the reference list. UCLA data is from the Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP). The study integrates data from 7 different acquisition sites, hence MULTI-SITE (N>=2) is also applicable.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We included neuroimaging datasets acquired from two tertiary hospitals in the Republic of Korea, the Asan Medical Center (AMC) and Jeonbuk National University Hospital (JNUH). Several publicly available neuroimaging datasets were used in this study. From the SchizConnect database ... we obtained Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE), Neuromorphometry by Computer Algorithm Chicago (NMorphCH), MIND Clinical Imaging Consortium (MCIC), and Function Biomedical Informatics Research Network (fBIRN) datasets. Neuroimaging and clinical data from University of California Los Angeles Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics LA5c Study (UCLA) were downloaded from OpenNeuro"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All seven datasets were combined after ComBat harmonization. PBSI scores were computed separately within HC and SCZ groups. The HC group's PBSI mean and SD were used to calculate z-scores for patients, enabling identification of 'deviant' patients (z-score < mean - 1.5 SD). This study does not train a traditional normative model but uses a normative approach to identify deviant patients based on healthy control distributions.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "We performed ComBat harmonization to adjust the site differences ... In the patient group, we calculated the z score of the PBSI score using the mean and S.D. of the PBSI scores in the control group. Using the z score of the PBSI score, we divided the patient group into 'deviant' and 'other patients' based on a criterion of lower than the mean -1.5 S.D."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study uses a PBSI-based normative approach rather than a traditional trained normative model. The 420 healthy controls constitute the reference group for computing normative PBSI distributions. There is no separate train/test split as PBSI is computed across all HC simultaneously. The z-scores are derived from the entire HC group's PBSI mean and SD.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age information is provided for the combined HC group across all 7 sites. Individual site-level age statistics are available in Table 1: AMC HC mean 30.9 (SD 5), COBRE HC mean 39.3 (SD 11.5), fBIRN HC mean 34.9 (SD 12.1), JNUH HC mean 37.9 (SD 12.1), MCIC HC mean 35.2 (SD 12.3), NMorphCH HC mean 31.7 (SD 8.5), UCLA HC mean 36 (SD 8.8). The overall values are weighted aggregates reported in Table 1. No train-phase exists as PBSI uses all HCs as reference simultaneously.
